title: Derivatives of trigonometric functions
goal: Differentiate the six trig functions ($\sin, \cos, \tan, \sec, \csc, \cot$) and use them to find tangent lines and horizontal peaks on wave graphs.

beforeThis.skill: Memory hook: thethree "co-" functions ($\cos x, \cot x, \csc x$) are the exact three whose derivatives pick up a minus sign!

seeIt.title: The Derivative of Trigonometric Functions
seeIt.creator: Dr. Trefor Bazett
seeIt.watchFor: Covers the derivatives of all six trig functions (with geometric intuition in 3Blue1Brown at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S0_qX4VJhMQ).

questions.asking: Spot the $x$-values on $[-2\pi, 2\pi]$ where $y = \sin x$ has a flat tangent line, and state what feature $y = \cos x$ has at those same $x$-values.
questions.statement: Graph sine and cosine on the same axes, from $x = -2\pi$ to $x = 2\pi$. Mark the points where $\sin x$ has a horizontal tangent. What do these points correspond to, on the graph of cosine?

questions.asking: Spot the $x$-values on $[-2\pi, 2\pi]$ where $y = \sin x$ is rising most steeply, and state what feature $y = \cos x$ has at those same $x$-values.
questions.statement: Graph sine and cosine on the same axes, from $x = -2\pi$ to $x = 2\pi$. Mark the points where $\sin x$ has a tangent line of maximum (positive) slope. What do these points correspond to, on the graph of cosine?

questions.asking: Check if taking four derivatives in a row returns the original function for $\sin x$, $\cos x$, and $\tan x$.
questions.statement:
Which statements below are true, and which false?

  1. $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}^4}{\mathrm{d}x^4} \sin x = \sin x$
  2. $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}^4}{\mathrm{d}x^4} \cos x = \cos x$
  3. $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}^4}{\mathrm{d}x^4} \tan x = \tan x$

questions.asking: Take the derivative $(\sin x + \cos x)' = \cos x - \sin x$, set it equal to $0$, and find all angles $x$ where $\sin x = \cos x$.
questions.statement: For which values of $x$ does the function $f(x) = \sin x + \cos x$ have a horizontal tangent?

questions.asking: Use the product rule on $e^x \cdot \cot x$, remembering that $(\cot x)' = -\csc^2 x$.
Find the constants $a$ and $b$ so that $\cos(x)$ and $ax + b$ have both the same height and the same slope at $x = 0$.
questions.statement:
Find the values of the constants $a$ and $b$ for which

$$f(x) = \begin{cases} \cos(x) & x \le 0 \\ ax + b & x > 0 \end{cases}$$

is differentiable everywhere.

questions.asking: Find the exact value of the limit by recognizing what derivative at $x = 2015$ this difference quotient represents.
Find the exact numerical value of the limit as $x \to \pi/3$ by relating the quotient to the derivative of $\cos x$ at $\pi/3$.
Find the exact numerical value of the limit as $x \to \pi$ by relating the quotient to the derivative of $\sin x$ at $\pi$.
Find the values of $a$ and $b$ that make the two branches of $f(x)$ match in both value and derivative at $x = 0$.
questions.statement:
The derivative of the function

$$f(x) = \begin{cases} ax + b & \text{for } x < 0 \\[6pt] \dfrac{6 \cos x}{2 + \sin x + \cos x} & \text{for } x \ge 0 \end{cases}$$

exists for all $x$. Determine the values of the constants $a$ and $b$.

questions.asking: Find the height $y_0 = \tan(\pi/4)$ and the slope $m = \sec^2(\pi/4)$, then plug both into the line formula $y = y_0 + m(x - \pi/4)$.
questions.statement: Find the equation of the line tangent to the graph of $y = \tan(x)$ at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

questions.asking: Plug $x = 0$ into $y$ to get the starting height $y_0$, plug $x = 0$ into $y'$ to get the slope $m$, and write $y = y_0 + mx$.
questions.statement: Find the equation of the line tangent to the graph of $y = \sin(x) + \cos(x) + e^x$ at $x = 0$.

questions.asking: Differentiate $e^x \sin x$ using the product rule, factor out $e^x$ (which is never $0$), and solve $\sin x + \cos x = 0$.
questions.statement: For which values of $x$ does the function $f(x) = e^x \sin x$ have a horizontal tangent line?
